newsitem.title: USA: U.S. welcomes ASEAN initiative on Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: U.S. welcomes ASEAN initiative on Cambodia.

text.p: The United States on Tuesday welcomed a decision by the Association of Southeast Asian Nations to try to help bring the Cambodian crisis to an end and urged other countries to back its effort strongly.

"The United States welcomes and strongly endorses ASEAN's decision, announced at the meeting yesterday, to remain engaged in seeking to restore political stability to Cambodia," State Department spokesman James Rubin told reporters.

"We share ASEAN's goal of restoring the principles of the Paris peace accords, and we believe that ASEAN is uniquely placed to sustain contact with Cambodia's principal political actors in pursuit of those goals."
Rubin called ASEAN "a model for regional efforts at cooperation and problem-solving" and said the initiative deserved the strong endorsement of other countries.

He said Washington would strongly support a future effort by ASEAN to organise an informal meeting of all parties to the Cambodian conflict, and he praised the organisation's readiness to provide technical support for national elections.

Cambodia's second prime minister, Hun Sen, now controls most of the country after ousting the first prime minister, Prince Norodom Ranariddh, in bloody fighting last month. The two sides are still battling in the northwest of the country.
Rubin said Washington had seen reports that Cambodia's King Sihanouk, Ranariddh's father, was prepared to abdicate but this was not the first time the possibility had been raised.

He said the United States was not taking a position on what "would clearly be a significant personal and political decision for the king," noting that Sihanouk was very popular and enjoyed significant influence in the country.
"We're not going to try to tell King Sihanouk what we think is the right thing to do in this case," Rubin said, adding, "To the extent we have a view, it needn't be expressed publicly."

Diplomatic sources said ASEAN foreign ministers agreed at a special meeting on Monday in Singapore to begin a mediation effort to restore stability in Cambodia, with general elections in May 1998 serving as the centrepiece of their efforts.

Ranariddh is abroad with many of his FUNCINPEC party leaders. Hun Sen has never been more than lukewarm to the idea of mediation by the nine-member ASEAN, which postponed Cambodia's entry after the fighting in Phnom Penh.
Rubin said Washington hoped other countries would join the United States in supporting the ASEAN intiative, which he called "an impresssive example of the organisation's influence and dynamism."
